clue.text: Complained of control by editor

parts.note: to have a grip on something is to have control of it

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about how tightly their editor keeps them in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is an informal verb for grumbling, so griped is a past-tense synonym of grumbled.

clue.text: Cattle disease from the Volga?

parts.note: the Volga is a Russian river; also the name of a tick-borne cattle illness

explanation.walkthrough: In the Cold War, 'red' meant Soviet or Russian, so the water of the Volga, a Russian river, is red water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick-borne cattle illness, babesiosis, makes the animals pass discoloured urine and bears this name.

clue.text: German appearing: kind of blue

explanation.surface: A German turns up in a particular shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the old north German state was a Prussian, and the deep blue pigment ferric ferrocyanide bears the same name.

clue.text: Down which our brainy types sometimes disappear?

definitions.text: Down which our brainy types sometimes disappear?

parts.words: Down which our brainy types sometimes disappear?
parts.note: plays on the brain drain, scientists leaving the country, as if they went down a pipe for waste water

explanation.walkthrough: The 'brain drain' was the emigration of British scientists, mostly to America, in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe carrying away rainwater or waste is something things vanish down, like brains in the brain drain.

clue.text: Convert the peony? Yes, do

indicators.note: to do something, as in doing one's hair, is to arrange it, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener is urged to transform a peony, and agrees enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' looks like the instruction to rearrange, but it is the definition; the shuffling is signalled by 'do' at the end, and 'Yes' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer to a religion is a recent convert, the original sense of the word.

clue.text: .We stand for these racial articles on a lady

parts.note: racial and national both relate to a people or nation
an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
Ms is the title of a woman

explanation.surface: We stand for these racial articles on a lady
explanation.walkthrough: 'We stand for these' reads as tolerating insults, but it means rising to our feet as the songs are played.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences rise to their feet when a country's patriotic songs are played.

clue.text: Ropy artist?.

parts.note: a poor artist could be called ropy, but the word sought is both a boat's mooring line and someone who paints

explanation.definitionFit: A rope at a boat's bow used for tying up has the same name as someone who makes pictures in oils.

clue.text: Pining for poor Nina Grey

indicators.note: poor suggests the names are in bad shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longs for poor Nina Grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pining and yearning are both a sad longing for something absent.

clue.text: Lift for, the Spanish girl on the hill

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
Eva is a girl's name
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl on a hill hitches a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American word for what the British call a lift.

clue.text: Administrative officer getting the bird

explanation.surface: An army staff officer is given a sharp dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: An army staff officer who assists a commander with administration bears this title, and it is also the name of a large Asian stork.

clue.text: Silver, say, for one to chatter about

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a piece of silver would be good for, then talks idly about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the sea-robber in Stevenson's Treasure Island; 'say' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the most famous fictional buccaneer, so he is an example of a sea robber.

clue.text: Role in which he took the lead

definitions.text: Role in which he took the lead

parts.words: Role in which he took the lead
parts.note: reads like a star actor's leading part, but refers to the Shakespeare suitor who wins Portia by choosing the lead casket

explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia's suitors choose between gold, silver and lead caskets; the successful suitor picks the lead one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian suitor in The Merchant of Venice is a stage part whose plot turns on choosing the casket of lead.

clue.text: Man reverses alphabetical order in poetic form

parts.note: Stan is a man's name

indicators.note: reverses tells us the A-to-Z pair is turned to run backwards

parts.note: the alphabet runs from A to Z

explanation.surface: A man flouts alphabetical order when composing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lines forming a unit of a poem is a verse, which is a poetic form.

clue.text: He causes trouble when a soldier volunteers to run

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A troublemaker appears when a soldier signs up to make a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rouser who stirs up unrest is someone who causes trouble.

clue.text: Chinese, perhaps, or 'aliens anyway, around the East End

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the final letter of East
anyway means in any manner, so the letters of or aliens may be put in any order
End points to the last letter of East

explanation.surface: Chinese people, or foreigners in general, gathered around London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional immigrant area of east London, which sells the surface; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Far East, of whom the Chinese are an example, were once called Orientals.

clue.text: One owed a Pole 37½ gallons — fishy!

parts.note: CR is short for creditor, a person to whom money is owed
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A lender demands his due from a Polish man over a suspicious quantity of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a geographical pole. The definition is a herring measure of 37½ gallons, so 'fishy' is the hint that the measure is for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This old Scottish measure of fresh herrings held about thirty-seven and a half gallons.

clue.text: Grunts in putting ball in pocket, and pays out

indicators.note: Grunts in, with the ball put in pocket, means both go inside the pocket

parts.note: a cup is a hollow, pocket-like holder
O is ball-shaped
ugh is a grunt of disgust, so grunts are UGHS

explanation.surface: A snooker player grunts as he pots a ball, and pays up his losses.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue ran into 16-down; the scan gives the full clue. 'in pocket' is the snooker picture of potting, and 'putting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cough up is an informal idiom for handing over money reluctantly.

clue.text: Unfortunately not a diet which produces a cure

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of not a diet are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, it is not dieting that brings about a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts a poison is a cure for it.

clue.text: Drag a river containing seaweed

indicators.note: containing says the letters sit inside the words Drag a river

explanation.surface: Dredging a river turns up seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: This jelly is extracted from red seaweed, so the word is used for the seaweed itself.

clue.text: Prior's climbing mountain to reach city on river

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the mountain is reversed

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily
Rio de Janeiro is the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A monk who heads a priory climbs a mountain to get to a riverside city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monk but is the adjective meaning earlier; the 's stands for 'is' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior means coming before in time or position, the same as prior.

clue.text: Debate Omar in his youth heard from Doctor and Saint

definitions.text: Omar in his youth heard from Doctor and Saint

explanation.surface: A literary allusion: what the poet Omar listened to as a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: In FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: 'Myself when young did eagerly frequent Doctor and Saint, and heard great argument'.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a reasoned dispute, and the Rubaiyat says young Omar heard 'great' such disputing from Doctor and Saint.

clue.text: Ariel not free in this story

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters of Ariel and not are liberated into a new order

explanation.surface: In The Tempest, the spirit Ariel is not yet freed in this tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel is the spirit Prospero promises to free, which makes 'free' read naturally as part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation can mean a narrative or account, as in the relating of a tale.

clue.text: Course artist takes on instrument, I conclude

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
the viol is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: An artist takes up an instrument, and someone sums up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a stage of a meal; 'takes on' and 'conclude' place the pieces in order with I at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed pasta parcels can be served as one part of a meal, a dish such as a starter.

clue.text: "Show his eyes; and —— his heart" (Macbeth)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the witches' chant over the line of kings in Macbeth, Act 4, needs a verb meaning to cause sorrow

explanation.walkthrough: The witches chant 'Show his eyes, and grieve his heart; come like shadows, so depart' as they show Macbeth the line of Banquo's kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the witches' line means to cause sorrow to the heart.

clue.text: Rumbles one with a point perhaps in workers' organizations

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the unions' abbreviation

parts.note: TUs are trade unions, organizations of workers

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of one, a and the point could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: N, for north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A lone man with a grievance stirs up trouble within the trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumbles' looks like a verb about noise or discovery, but it is a plural noun: rumble seats at the back of old cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear passenger compartment of an early motor car, like a dickey or rumble seat, was called a tonneau.

clue.text: Said to be pinched from the branch

indicators.note: Said tells us we want a word that sounds like the theft word when spoken

parts.note: to be pinched is to be taken by theft, which is stolen

explanation.surface: Someone claims a cutting was nicked from the branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner or creeping shoot from a plant, a type of offshoot, is a stolon in botany.

clue.text: Inspector was formerly an underground worker

parts.note: ex- means former or formerly
an is the indefinite article, here A
a miner works below ground

explanation.surface: A government inspector turns out to have once worked down a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner checks or scrutinises things, as an inspector does.

clue.text: Forward commander has deserted — oh dear!

indicators.note: has deserted means the commander leaves, so his letters are taken away

parts.note: a forward child is precocious, advanced beyond its years
CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: A soldier laments that the forward commander has gone absent without leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a military position but means precocious; removing CO leaves the word. 'oh dear' is read as a vocative address to a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressing someone as precious, like darling, is calling them dear.

clue.text: Supports depression in some ways

indicators.note: in places the depression inside the ways

parts.note: ST is street, a way, so several ways are STS
a rut is a depression or groove in a road

explanation.surface: Ruts in some roads hold up traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Struts are braces or props that hold a structure up, so they are supports.
